To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) political liberalism is a promising theory for dealing with the problem of unreasonable views in liberal democratic societies; (2) political liberals have to take seriously the idea that there are limits to the toleration of unreasonable views in a well-ordered liberal democratic society; (3) there are good reasons to prevent unreasonable views from becoming widespread, and to prevent unreasonable people from acting upon unreasonable views; (4) the prevention of the unreasonable can be done without violating the basic principles of political liberalism;
the political liberal approach to containing unreasonable beliefs and behavior raises some significant worries.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liberal state should be prepared to contain unreasonable beliefs and behaviors, but that it is not clear that it should do so in the manner proposed by Quong.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

political liberals should not only be concerned with the containment of unreasonable beliefs but also with the containment of the disrespectful and devaluing attitudes that underlie them, and that this should be done in a way that is respectful to those who hold such views.
political liberalism is not a good framework for thinking about the containment of unreasonable beliefs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the political liberal approach to the containment of unreasonable views is in need of significant revision.
political liberals need to be much more aware of the ways in which their approach to the containment of unreasonable views is likely to affect relations between reasonable and unreasonable citizens.
